description: Multi-Provider Translation Engine - Create the provider abstraction layer that allows users to choose how their text is translated: (1) Built-in MarianMT models (free), (2) Bring-Your-Own-Key for OpenAI/HuggingFace/Google Translate, (3) Pay admin credits to use admin-managed API keys. Includes new SQLAlchemy models, provider service layer, credit system, and updated translate endpoint.
steps: Create src/api/models/__init__.py with DeclarativeBase. Create src/api/models/user.py (User model with id, email, password_hash, is_admin, credits_balance, created_at). Create src/api/models/api_key.py (APIKey model). Create src/api/models/usage_log.py (UsageLog model). These files are currently referenced but do not exist physically.

Create src/api/models/provider_key.py - Model for user-stored provider API keys (user_id, provider enum [openai, huggingface, google, deepl], encrypted_api_key, label, created_at). Create src/api/models/admin_provider_key.py - Model for admin-managed provider keys (provider, encrypted_api_key, is_active, usage_count).
Create src/api/models/credit_transaction.py - Model for credit purchase/debit tracking (user_id, amount, transaction_type [purchase, debit, refund], description, created_at).

Create src/api/services/providers/__init__.py with a base TranslationProvider abstract class (async def translate(text, source_lang, target_lang) -> str). Create src/api/services/providers/marianmt.py - wraps existing worker HTTP call. Create src/api/services/providers/openai_provider.py - calls OpenAI GPT-4/3.5 for translation. Create src/api/services/providers/huggingface_provider.py - calls HuggingFace Inference API. Create src/api/services/providers/google_provider.py - calls Google Cloud Translation API.

Create src/api/services/provider_manager.py - ProviderManager class that: (a) resolves which provider to use based on request params, (b) handles BYOK vs admin-credit logic, (c) deducts credits for admin-key usage, (d) instantiates the correct provider with the right API key.

Create src/api/routers/providers.py - endpoints for users to manage their provider keys: POST /api/v1/providers/keys (store a key), GET /api/v1/providers/keys (list keys), DELETE /api/v1/providers/keys/{id}, GET /api/v1/providers (list available providers with pricing info).

Update src/api/routers/translate.py - extend TranslateRequest to accept optional provider field (marianmt|openai|huggingface|google) and optional provider_key_id. When provider is specified, route through ProviderManager instead of directly to worker. Default remains marianmt (free).
Create src/api/routers/credits.py - endpoints for credit management: GET /api/v1/credits/balance, POST /api/v1/credits/purchase (mock payment for now, adds credits), GET /api/v1/credits/transactions.
Update src/shared/config.py - add admin_openai_key, admin_huggingface_key, admin_google_key, credit_cost_per_1k_chars settings.
Register new routers in src/api/main.py (providers, credits).
Update pyproject.toml to add openai and google-cloud-translate dependencies.
acceptance_criteria: TranslateRequest accepts optional provider and provider_key_id fields
Users can store their own API keys for OpenAI, HuggingFace, and Google via /api/v1/providers/keys
Translation using built-in MarianMT still works as default (no breaking change)
Provider abstraction cleanly supports adding new providers in the future
Credit system allows users to check balance and view transactions
Admin keys in config can be used when user pays credits
All new models have proper SQLAlchemy async patterns matching existing code style
verification: Run pytest tests/ -v to confirm existing tests still pass
Run python -c 'from src.api.services.providers import MarianMTProvider, OpenAIProvider, HuggingFaceProvider, GoogleProvider' to verify imports work
Run python -c 'from src.api.models import Base; print(Base.metadata.tables.keys())' to verify all models are registered
findings: Models directory had to be un-ignored from .gitignore (models/ rule intended for ML binaries was blocking src/api/models/). Fixed with negation rule. test_api.py tests have pre-existing errors related to mock.patch not finding src.api.main module - verified same failures on base state without any changes. Python 3.12 used (3.9 was the default but project requires >=3.11). All new imports verified working. Provider abstraction uses abstract base class pattern for clean extensibility.
